_comment_about_this_file: Managed-policy template for Microsoft Edge. Edge uses the same
ExtensionSettings + ExtensionInstallForcelist policy keys as Chrome,
but under the Microsoft\Edge registry/policy hive rather than
Edge extension IDs are different from Chrome IDs even for the same
extension package. If sourcing from the Edge Add-ons store, the ID is
on the listing page. See docs/enterprise/DEPLOYMENT.md.

_comment_about_settings: Identical to the Chrome template's settings block - same keys,
same meanings, same code reading them. chrome-managed-policy.json
in this directory carries the long-form commentary; the short
enforceTimeoutMs. Accepted and then ignored, so deliberately
allowedProviders takes CATALOG PROVIDER IDS from
shared/ai-surfaces.json; the accepted values are the enum in
managed-schema.json. `[]` or unset means every catalog surface is
screened - the default, and the recommended setting. A non-empty
list only ever REMOVES surfaces from screening, and a provider
left off it is not screened at all: prompts to it leave the
enforceTimeoutMs is the fail-closed ceiling. A held request that
gets no verdict inside it is BLOCKED, so this value must exceed
worst-case screening time on the slowest machine in the fleet.
